content.title: What is Aged Care?
content.text: What is Aged Care?Aged Care refers to various forms of support for people that are ageing and need help performing routine activities for themselves or their home. It can include everyday activities such as groceries and shopping, cooking and house chores, medical-related activities such as going to the doctor, getting prescriptions and refills or doing physiotherapy, personal care such as bathing, dressing, walking or keeping fit, or minor home improvements and installation of special support equipment such as handrails, ramps, walking frames and bathroom rails. If the people are unable to live on their own and take care of themselves properly, accommodation is also part of the Aged Care program, and nursing homes are involved in this project. Aged Care LegislationThe main law that sets out the standards and expectations of Aged Care in Australia is the Aged Care 1997, which includes rules and regulations about funding, regulation, fees and eligibility, quality of care, patients’ right and non-compliance. This law and all its consequent amendments aim to provide a respectful and dignified treatment to senior citizens, without any discrimination based on sex, colour, social background, religious beliefs and psychological state. The services provided have to respect quality standards and are constantly checked through ongoing assessments and monitoring processes. Nursing homes are regularly visited by the Aged Care Quality and Safety Commission, and constant feedbacks from care recipients are collected and analysed. Complaints can be filed to the same Commission, and providers are expected to keep up with new regulations and to provide improvement plans.Eligibility and financial considerations Senior citizens are eligible for government-funded aged care services if they are at least 65 years old and need help performing basic activities, however Aboriginal or Torres Strait Islander people may qualify when 50 years old. The Australian Government sets a maximum fee per Aged Care day, and these fees are income-tested and means-tested. Once approved and assigned to a specific economical category, the patient cannot be asked for higher fees. If the provider intends to increase their fees or charge for extra activities, an approval will be required from the Aged Care Pricing Commissioner. The Commonwealth Home Support Program helps senior citizens in need of entry-level support in their own homes, while the fees for residential care in Aged Care homes, or nursing homes, is determined based on the patient’s financial income and assets assessment.
